markdown_report:
At 0% progress, prioritize a small SASRec extension with independently measurable components. No validation gains are established.

**Insights from the starting point.** (1) SASRec already represents ordered context through causal attention. A residual interest summary can test persistent preferences without replacing the backbone [1]. (2) Users report broadly related recommendations and excessive influence from occasional purchases. Repeated recent evidence may identify narrower preferences, but cannot establish equipment ownership, compatibility, or satisfied needs. (3) Electronics has 14.95% sampled wrong rankings and a −0.4812 tenth-percentile margin. These identify weak training separation; embedding scores near 0.5 provide little evidence of severe collapse. Neither diagnostic establishes validation performance.

**Insights from related work.** (1) MISER separates multiple interests and temporal changes [2], motivating a lightweight persistent-history branch; recurrence-weighted cosine pooling remains an unverified adaptation. (2) eSASRec motivates testing candidate-set cross entropy [3], although its combined results do not isolate the objective. (3) R2NS motivates delaying hard negatives [4]. Uniform sampling provides a simpler first experiment. (4) ReZero supports zero-initialized residual gates [5]; explicitly bounding the added vector is still necessary. Popularity research motivates checking whether apparent recurrence instead reflects item frequency or embedding density [6].

**Framework and directions.** Organize interventions along three axes: evidence aggregation, ranking supervision, and content grounding. SASRec supplies ordered aggregation; recency and recurrence pooling add history evidence; multiple negatives strengthen supervision; title encoders potentially add grounding. Across these axes, distinguish observed interactions from inferred intent. Compatibility, ownership, and satisfied needs remain unobserved and must not become fabricated labels.

**Candidate ideas.** Scores are originality/future potential/user alignment/model alignment/code difficulty; higher difficulty means harder implementation.

- **Recurrence-gated residual SASRec with uniform multi-negative candidate-set CE: 4/6/7/8/6.** Originality: targeted integration, established ingredients. Potential: reusable evidence gate, unverified persistence interpretation. User alignment: targets broad matches and isolated-purchase dominance, cannot verify compatibility. Model alignment: tests weak separation, retains false-negative risk. Difficulty: small architecture, substantial causal masking, sampling, and export safeguards.
- **Scratch-trained title residual: 4/6/7/5/5.** Originality: simple feature fusion, familiar design. Potential: content grounding, sparse text supervision. User alignment: narrower terminology, superficial overlap remains. Model alignment: may separate confusing items, unproven. Difficulty: modest encoder, additional vocabulary artifacts.
- **Warm-started moderate-hard negatives: 4/7/4/9/5.** Originality: known curriculum, task-specific adaptation. Potential: difficult rankings, sampling sensitivity. User alignment: indirect relevance benefits, no explicit preference evidence. Model alignment: targets margin tails, false-negative risk. Difficulty: manageable sampling, extra scoring cost [4].

**Selected algorithm.** Retain the recurrence-gated residual as a hypothesis, with recency-only pooling as its essential simpler comparator. For each causal prefix, measure each history item's support from distinct earlier item IDs using normalized embedding cosine similarity; average at most three strongest matches. Deduplicate support evidence and cap each item's pooling contribution. Learn nonnegative support and recency coefficients, then add a projected summary through a zero-initialized scalar gate. Explicitly cap the residual norm at 25% of the backbone feature norm. This targets broad relevance and isolated-purchase dominance; multi-negative CE targets weak positive–negative separation. It does not directly solve unsupported compatibility assumptions or redundant replacements.

Use 32 independent uniform negatives with replacement, rejecting padding and every item in the user's complete training history. Preserve duplicates. Because the diagnosis loader yields user=None, implement exclusion inside the training sampler while user identity is available; truncated sequences cannot supply complete exclusions. Call the objective candidate-set CE, without importance correction or a full-softmax claim. Fix temperature to 1 initially.

Predeclare baseline, loss-only, recency-residual, and recurrence-residual comparisons; the residual variants share the same CE objective. Preserve a residual-only comparison with the baseline loss if budget permits. Diagnose recurrence using uniform pooling, frequency-matched shuffled histories, a training-frequency score, support–frequency/background-cosine correlations, and target-frequency strata. These are controls, not new selection metrics; failure to distinguish recurrence from recency limits the interpretation.

Select exclusively by pinned four-category macro validation HR@10, with a fixed checkpoint schedule and no open-ended tuning. Where evaluator outputs permit, bootstrap paired user hits within each category and average category differences equally [7]. Intervals condition on fixed candidates and omit seed variability and adaptive-selection bias [8]. One additional hit changes macro HR by 0.125 percentage points. Sampled gains do not establish full-catalog gains [9]. Preserve seeds, routing, splits, the 200-epoch environment default, and diagnosis/predictor contracts; charge every run against the shared budget.

idea.description: Recurrence-gated residual SASRec with uniform multi-negative candidate-set cross entropy. Preserve causal SASRec, add an explicitly norm-bounded history summary, and test whether recurrence weighting improves on simpler recency pooling. Independently evaluate the objective before attributing gains to the representation.
idea.motivation: The user diagnosis identifies broadly related recommendations and excessive influence from occasional purchases as distinct failures. Recurrence-supported pooling explicitly tests whether sustained recent evidence improves narrow preference matching. Electronics exhibits weak lower-tail training margins, motivating stronger candidate discrimination. These are hypotheses: learned cosine support can reflect popularity or dense embedding regions, and repeated purchases can reflect redundancy rather than persistent intent. The method cannot establish ownership, compatibility, complementarity, or whether a need is satisfied.
idea.implementation_notes:
Retain the baseline SASRec architecture, optimizer, data mappings, splits, and batching unless explicitly ablated. For the recurrence branch, normalize item embeddings only for support calculations; keep the baseline scoring geometry unchanged. At timestep t, use only valid positions j <= t. For each such position j, compute support against distinct earlier item IDs, excluding the same item ID and duplicate evidence. Average the top min(3, eligible_count) cosine similarities; use zero when no eligible evidence exists. Deduplicate pooling contributions within each prefix by retaining the most recent occurrence of each item ID. Compute masked softmax weights from a * support_j - b * (t-j), with a and b parameterized by softplus and initialized to 1 and 0.1. Positions rather than timestamps define recency in this experiment. Renormalize weights over eligible positions and return zero for empty histories. Project the pooled vector using a randomly initialized bias-free linear layer. Bound its norm relative to the corresponding SASRec feature: r_bounded = r * min(1, 0.25 * norm(h) / max(norm(r), 1e-8)). Use h_prime = h + tanh(g) * r_bounded with scalar g initialized exactly to zero. The gate learns first; branch parameters receive useful gradients after the gate moves away from zero. The 0.25 cap is a fixed initial design choice, not an established optimum. Use identical features and shared scoring in training, validation, prediction, and diagnostics. Recency-only uses the identical branch with a fixed to zero; uniform pooling fixes both coefficients to zero. Freeze these definitions before comparing variants.

Initially use K=32 independent uniform negatives with replacement and temperature 1. Sample from each user's catalog complement after excluding padding and the complete observed training history, including the target. Modify the sampler internally to retain user identity during sampling, while preserving diagnosis batches as (None, sequence, positive, negative) with B x L tensors. The training step may obtain additional negatives through a private sampler interface; do not infer complete histories from truncated sequences. Preserve duplicate draws. If a user's eligible complement is empty, skip that user's supervised examples consistently and report the count; never draw a known positive. Seed Python, NumPy, PyTorch, sampling generators, and loader workers deterministically with training seed 42, and retain preprocessing seed 0. Never use validation or test interactions for exclusions. Unknown positives remain possible false negatives.

Compute cross entropy over [positive, K negatives], with target column zero. This is a candidate-set objective and needs no sampling-probability correction. It is not a full-catalog softmax approximation. If a corrected partition objective is later tested, declare it separately: subtract log(K*q_u) from negative logits only, leave the deterministic positive uncorrected, and describe the restricted partition and biased log-loss estimator. Do not silently mix these objectives. For memory, chunk valid positions before candidate scoring, accumulate summed CE normalized by the total valid-position count, and use activation checkpointing around chunk scoring/loss to avoid retaining all candidate activations. Merely summing ordinary chunk losses retains their graphs. Use a PyTorch checkpoint API supported by the installed version. Benchmark its compute cost against the shared budget.

Preserve DiagnosisProbe(view, device).run_full_diagnosis(train_loader), returning metrics and metric_definitions. view.model references the actual trained module; view.item_emb remains accessible; view.log2feats and view.predict_score include the complete selected scoring path. Preserve the public diagnostic loader shape even when training uses richer sampler internals. Compute raw-logit margins on fixed diagnostic examples and negatives across variants, but acknowledge that objective changes can change logit scale. Report unavailable category breakdowns explicitly; never fabricate metadata. Only histories, timestamps, titles, and descriptions are available. No review content, ratings, prices, stores, item categories, simulator traits, external datasets, or pretrained weights may be used.

Serialize architecture configuration, vocabulary or other required artifacts if used, and checkpoint under the trial directory. Update the predictor writer so working/predict.py reconstructs the exact selected architecture and routes all four datasets correctly. Keep DATA_DIR = os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR'], preprocessing seed 0, training seed 42, single-GPU execution, and int(os.environ.get('SASREC_EPOCHS', '200')). Preserve baseline validation cadence and checkpoint-selection rules consistently across variants; record them in artifacts. The pinned host evaluator remains authoritative.

Predeclare baseline, loss-only, recency-residual plus CE, and recurrence-residual plus CE comparisons. Include recurrence-residual with the baseline objective if budget permits to complete the original representation/objective ablation. Use equal epoch limits and report actual GPU time, because equal epochs need not imply equal cost. Reserve budget before starting each experiment and charge training, diagnostics, debugging, and failures against 43,200 GPU-seconds. Prefer the simpler variant when evidence for recurrence is weak. Use low-cost frozen-model controls where possible: uniform pooling, training-frequency scoring, and deterministic frequency-matched history shuffling using training-derived frequency bins. These interventions are sensitivity checks and can introduce distribution shift; they do not establish causality. Measure support correlation with log training frequency and mean cosine to a fixed sample of training catalog items. A background-cosine-subtracted support variant is optional and must count as an additional declared trial. Report target-frequency-stratified validation results descriptively when compatible outputs are available; avoid searching strata for favorable findings.

Select only by pinned macro validation HR@10, retaining every category. If the evaluator exposes paired per-user hit indicators, compute a 95% paired bootstrap interval from 10,000 resamples with a fixed bootstrap seed, independently resampling users within each category and averaging the four category differences equally. Do not modify the evaluator to obtain these outputs. Such intervals condition on the fixed candidate sets, omit training-seed variability, and do not correct adaptive validation selection. Limit the predeclared comparison set and checkpoint schedule. Training-margin improvements are diagnostics; sampled HR gains do not prove full-catalog improvements for the twenty-user simulator.
idea.pseudocode:
Keep all four baseline dataset mappings, splits, and routing.
Set preprocessing seed=0; seed training and sampler/worker generators with 42.
Use SASREC_EPOCHS from the environment, defaulting to 200.
Predeclare variants and checkpoint schedule; reserve GPU budget per run.

Sampler, while user identity is available:
    eligible_u = catalog minus padding minus complete_training_history[u]
    if eligible_u is empty: skip and count supervised examples
    sample K=32 negatives independently and uniformly with replacement
    preserve duplicate draws and never consult held-out interactions
    expose baseline-shaped batches to diagnosis through an adapter

For each training batch:
    h = sasrec_backbone(sequence)
    if history_branch_enabled:
        e = normalize(item_embeddings(sequence), eps=1e-8)
        for each valid causal prefix ending at t:
            pool_positions = most_recent_occurrence_per_item(sequence[:t+1])
            for j in pool_positions:
                earlier = distinct valid item IDs before j, excluding sequence[j]
                k = min(3, number_of_earlier_items)
                support[j] = mean(top_k(cosine(e[j], earlier))) if k > 0 else 0
            logits = a * support[j] - b * (t-j)
            weights = masked_softmax(logits over pool_positions)
            pooled[t] = weighted sum of raw item embeddings, or zero if empty
        r = bias_free_projection(pooled)
        r = r * min(1, 0.25 * norm(h) / clamp_min(norm(r), 1e-8))
        features = h + tanh(g) * r       # initialize g=0
    else:
        features = h
    total_valid = count(valid positive positions)
    if total_valid == 0: continue
    loss = sum(checkpointed_chunk_CE(features, positives, K_negatives, temperature=1)) / total_valid
    # Each chunk forms [positive, negatives], target column zero; no q correction.
    backward(loss)
    optimizer.step()

Run unchanged pinned validation at the predeclared checkpoints.
Compare baseline, CE-only, recency+CE, and recurrence+CE by macro HR@10.
If budget permits, add recurrence with baseline loss and the declared controls.
Record frequency/density diagnostics without treating them as selection objectives.
Where paired hit outputs are available, bootstrap within category and average four deltas equally.
Export selected checkpoint, configuration, and matching predictor implementation.
Run DiagnosisProbe through the same feature and scoring paths.

originality.positive: Integrates recurrence-supported aggregation, an explicitly bounded residual, and controlled objective ablations around the observed user failures.
originality.negative: Recency pooling, cosine support, residual gates, and multi-negative cross entropy are established components; no new theoretical mechanism or demonstrated gain is established.

future_potential.positive: Provides a compact experimental foundation for separating recent context, repeated evidence, and later locally trained content grounding.
future_potential.negative: Recurrence may add little beyond recency and may encode popularity, semantic density, or redundant purchases rather than persistent intent.

code_difficulty.positive: Retains the SASRec backbone and requires only a small additional scoring branch.
code_difficulty.negative: Exact user-history exclusion, causal deduplication, bounded residuals, memory-safe multi-negative scoring, diagnostic adaptation, and predictor parity create meaningful implementation work.

related_work.title: Self-Attentive Sequential Recommendation
contributions: Uses causal self-attention, residual connections, and normalization for sequential recommendation.
Provides the starting backbone and shared item-scoring interface [1].
limitations: The supplied diagnosis identifies confusing candidate rankings in the trained baseline.
Attention patterns do not establish compatibility, ownership, satisfied needs, or a causal persistent-interest interpretation.

related_work.title: MISER
contributions: The supplied search summary describes multiple-interest modeling, temporal changes, and contrastive interest separation.
Motivates distinguishing persistent evidence from recent context [2].
limitations: Does not establish improvements for this benchmark or the proposed recurrence residual.
Multiple interests alone do not identify expired or satisfied needs.

related_work.title: eSASRec
contributions: The supplied search summary reports a competitive combination of sequential supervision, LiGR layers, and sampled softmax.
Motivates a controlled objective ablation [3].
limitations: Combined results do not isolate the objective's contribution.
Benefits under the pinned RecHarness protocol remain untested.

related_work.title: R2NS
contributions: The supplied search summary describes uniform warm-start, candidate recall, and curriculum re-ranking.
Motivates introducing negative hardness cautiously [4].
limitations: Hard negatives add scoring cost and false-negative risk.
The proposed initial experiment uses uniform negatives and does not reproduce the complete method.

related_work.title: ReZero
contributions: Supports zero-initialized scalar residual gates as an optimization technique [5].
limitations: Does not establish recommendation gains for this history branch.
A scalar gate alone does not bound residual magnitude relative to backbone features.

related_work.title: Popularity-amplification analysis
contributions: The supplied search summary describes popularity information in the principal spectrum of recommendation scores.
Motivates frequency and embedding-density controls [6].
limitations: Does not directly prove that recurrence pooling exploits popularity in this task.
Correlational controls cannot by themselves establish personalized intent.

related_work.title: SciPy bootstrap documentation
contributions: Documents paired resampling using shared indices.
Supports the paired, within-category uncertainty procedure [7].
limitations: The macro statistic requires equal category weighting.
Intervals omit variability from fixed candidate draws and training seeds.

related_work.title: On Over-fitting in Model Selection and Subsequent Selection Bias in Performance Evaluation
contributions: Explains overfitting of model-selection criteria and resulting evaluation bias.
Motivates a limited, predeclared comparison and checkpoint schedule [8].
limitations: Ordinary paired bootstrap intervals do not correct adaptive selection bias.
A fixed training seed does not eliminate validation overfitting.

related_work.title: On Sampled Metrics for Item Recommendation
contributions: Shows that sampled recommendation metrics can disagree with full-catalog rankings.
Limits interpretation of pinned sampled HR@10 gains [9].
limitations: Does not invalidate the required benchmark selection objective.
Does not establish full-catalog performance for any proposed variant.

related_work.title: Original SASRec sampler
contributions: Rejects items in the user's complete training history when drawing negatives.
Provides a reference for sampler-side exclusions while user identity is available.
limitations: Independent draws can repeat negatives.
Excluding known positives does not eliminate unknown false negatives.

related_work.title: Candidate Sampling
contributions: Defines candidate-sampling distributions and correction concepts.
Supports distinguishing candidate-set CE from importance-corrected objectives.
limitations: Corrections depend on the exact sampling scheme and objective.
A partition estimate does not make its logarithm an unbiased full-softmax loss.

related_work.title: Positive-inclusion correction
contributions: The supplied search summary distinguishes deterministic positive inclusion from sampled negatives.
Motivates leaving the positive uncorrected in the separately described restricted-partition estimator.
limitations: The initial proposed candidate-set CE experiment does not use this estimator.
The corrected restricted partition excludes known training positives and is not the full-catalog partition.
